General Textual and Methodological Disclosures
The front matter of The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition articulates several editorial policies and procedural standards that directly govern how the printed Greek text was constituted and how apparatus entries must be interpreted
1
more_horiz
:
Editorial Baseline and Collation Method:
The starting point was the 1881 text of Westcott and Hort (WH), adjusted to the edition's orthographical standards
1
2
.
This baseline was collated against three other primary editions: Samuel Tregelles (Treg, 1857–1879), the Greek text underlying the New International Version reconstructed by Goodrich and Lukaszewski (NIV, 2003), and the Byzantine Textform of Maurice Robinson and William Pierpont (RP, 2005)
1
more_horiz
.
Points of universal four-way agreement were tentatively accepted; disagreements were critically evaluated
2
. In 56 variation units across the New Testament, the editor adopted a variant not found in any of the four primary reference editions (38 of which were supported by marginal readings in WH, Treg, or Nestle-Aland)
2
6
.
The SBLGNT departs from the modern standard text (NA26–27/UBS3–4) in over 540 variation units
7
8
.
Orthography, Accents, and Breathings:
Both the printed text and the apparatus entries are systematically conformed to the orthography of the Bauer-Danker-Arndt-Gingrich lexicon (BDAG, 3rd ed.), overriding the spelling of the source editions
3
more_horiz
.
Orthographic differences (such as movable consonants or vowel interchanges) are explicitly excluded from the apparatus
3
10
.
Elision, crasis, movable ν, and interchanges between first and second aorist verb endings follow Westcott and Hort
10
.
Breathings on pronouns are treated as interpretive decisions: following a minority view of the UBS Editorial Committee (Bruce Metzger on Philippians 3:21), the edition occasionally prints rough breathings on forms of αὐτός when reflexive meaning is intended
9
.
Punctuation, Capitalization, and Paragraphing:
Punctuation generally adheres to Westcott and Hort, except where altered by textual decisions or NRSV paragraphing
11
. Where WH printed two consecutive punctuation marks (e.g., a comma beside a dash), these were reduced to a single mark
11
.
A high point (·) is systematically added before direct speech if no other punctuation mark is present
11
.
Capitalization follows Holmes's edition of The Apostolic Fathers (3rd ed.), capitalizing the first word of a paragraph, the first word of direct speech, and proper nouns
12
.
Verse numbering follows NA/UBS
12
; paragraph boundaries follow the NRSV, with syntactic conflicts resolved contextually
11
.
Apparatus Scope and Restraint on Brackets:
The apparatus documents 6,928 variation units, citing WH, Treg, NIV, and RP for every unit, while NA is cited only when it diverges from NIV
8
13
.
Single square brackets ([ ]) indicating doubtful text are restricted to six instances in the entire New Testament (Luke 22:19–20; 24:40; 24:51; 24:52; Eph 1:1; Col 1:20)
13
14
. Holmes argues that brackets have been overused to avoid difficult decisions and introduce an inherent bias toward inclusion (since an omission cannot be bracketed)
13
.
Double brackets around WH (〚WH〛) designate ancient passages that Westcott and Hort placed within double brackets as non-original material of historical interest
15
16
.
Analysis of the 12 B001 Targets
1. Romans 4:3 / Genesis 15:6
Locator: Page 317
17
.
Printed Text: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει; Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
17
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 3)
18
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Opens with a rhetorical question terminated by a Greek question mark (;), followed immediately by direct speech
17
. In accordance with the edition's rule, direct speech begins with a capital letter (Ἐπίστευσεν)
12
17
.
Syntax: Incorporates the postpositive conjunction δὲ directly into the citation clause (Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ...), coordinating the quotation with the preceding argument
17
.
2. Romans 9:25 / Hosea 2:23
Locator: Page 326
19
.
Printed Text: ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει· Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου καὶ τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην·
19
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 25)
20
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Contains an explicit prophetic attribution formula (ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει·) marked by a high point (·) before direct speech
11
19
. Direct speech is capitalized (Καλέσω)
12
19
.
Orthography: The prophet's name is accented and aspirated as Ὡσηὲ
19
.
Syntax & Lexis: Two parallel accusative phrases where the negative particles οὐ and οὐκ function as proclitic attributive modifiers modifying nominal and participial designations (τὸν οὐ λαόν μου, τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην), followed by predicate complements (λαόν μου, ἠγαπημένην)
19
.
3. Romans 9:26 / Hosea 1:10
Locator: Page 326
19
.
Printed Text: καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη ⸀αὐτοῖς· Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς, ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος.
19
Apparatus Entry: 26 αὐτοῖς WH NIV RP ] – Treg
20
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Variant: Textual variation unit on the indirect object pronoun ⸀αὐτοῖς in the introductory clause; Holmes prints αὐτοῖς with WH, NIV, and RP, whereas Tregelles omits it (– Treg)
19
20
.
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Introduced by the passive construction ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη ⸀αὐτοῖς· ending with a high point (·)
11
19
. Direct speech opens with a capital letter (Οὐ)
12
19
.
Syntax: Quotation text is unanimous across all reference editions; the relative locative phrase ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ is resumed demonstratively by ἐκεῖ inside the quotation
19
20
.
4. Romans 10:11 / Isaiah 28:16
Locator: Page 327
21
.
Printed Text: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.
21
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 11)
22
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Scriptural attribution formula λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· terminated by a high point (·)
11
21
. Direct speech begins with a capital letter (Πᾶς)
12
21
.
Orthography: Uses elision with an apostrophe before the rough breathing pronoun (ἐπʼ αὐτῷ), following WH convention
10
21
.
Syntax & Lexis: Features the universal quantifier Πᾶς modifying the substantival participle phrase ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ, followed by the simple negative οὐ with the future passive verb καταισχυνθήσεται
21
.
5. Romans 10:13 / Joel 2:32
Locator: Page 327
21
.
Printed Text: Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.
21
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 13)
22
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Syntax: Operates without a formal citation introductory verb; the quotation is integrated into Paul's syntax through the postpositive explanatory conjunction γάρ (Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν...)
21
.
Punctuation & Capitalization: Sentence opens with a capital letter (Πᾶς)
12
21
.
Syntax: Uses the indefinite relative construction ὃς ἂν governing an aorist middle subjunctive (ἐπικαλέσηται), followed by the anarthrous genitive κυρίου in the noun phrase τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου
21
.
6. Romans 11:34 / Isaiah 40:13
Locator: Page 329.
Printed Text: Τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου; ἢ τίς σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο;
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 34).
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Syntax: Seamlessly integrated into Paul's doxological discourse via the postpositive conjunction γάρ without an introductory citation formula.
Punctuation: Formatted as two coordinate rhetorical questions, each closed by a Greek question mark (;)
11
.
Lexis: Employs the noun phrase νοῦν κυρίου (accusative νοῦν rather than πνεῦμα).
7. Romans 15:12 / Isaiah 11:10
Locator: Page 334
23
.
Printed Text: καὶ πάλιν Ἠσαΐας λέγει· Ἔσται ἡ ῥίζα τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, καὶ ὁ ἀνιστάμενος ἄρχειν ἐθνῶν· ἐπʼ αὐτῷ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.
23
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 12).
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Iterative attribution formula καὶ πάλιν Ἠσαΐας λέγει· closed with a high point (·)
11
23
. Direct speech opens with a capital letter (Ἔσται)
12
23
.
Orthography: Elision with apostrophe in ἐπʼ αὐτῷ
10
23
; movable nu printed on the future verb ἐλπιοῦσιν following WH practice
10
23
.
Syntax: Tripartite quotation: a future existential clause (Ἔσται ἡ ῥίζα τοῦ Ἰεσσαί), a substantival participial phrase with an infinitive complement (καὶ ὁ ἀνιστάμενος ἄρχειν ἐθνῶν·), and an independent future clause (ἐπʼ αὐτῷ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν) punctuated by an intermediate high point
11
23
.
8. 1 Corinthians 1:19 / Isaiah 29:14
Locator: Page 339
24
.
Printed Text: γέγραπται γάρ· Ἀπολῶ τὴν σοφίαν τῶν σοφῶν, καὶ τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν ἀθετήσω.
24
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 19).
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Standard formula γέγραπται γάρ· followed by a high point (·)
11
24
. Direct speech begins with a capital letter (Ἀπολῶ)
12
24
.
Syntax & Lexis: Two coordinate parallel clauses conjoined by καί, balanced with first-person singular future active verbs: the contract future Ἀπολῶ and the liquid future ἀθετήσω
24
.
9. 1 Corinthians 6:16 / Genesis 2:24
Locator: Page 344
25
.
Printed Text: ⸀ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ὁ κολλώμενος τῇ πόρνῃ ἓν σῶμά ἐστιν; Ἔσονται γάρ, φησίν, οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν.
25
Apparatus Entry: 16 ἦ WH Treg NIV ] – RP
26
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Variant: Textual variation unit on the verse-initial disjunctive particle: Holmes prints ἦ with WH, Tregelles, and NIV, while Robinson–Pierpont (RP Byzantine textform) omits it (– RP)
26
.
Citation Formula: Uses the parenthetical attribution verb φησίν, placed between the coordinating conjunction γάρ and the subject οἱ δύο (Ἔσονται γάρ, φησίν, οἱ δύο...)
25
.
Punctuation & Capitalization: Preceding rhetorical question ends with a question mark (;), causing the quotation clause to begin with a capital letter (Ἔσονται)
11
more_horiz
.
Syntax: The quotation text proper (οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν) is unanimous across all collated editions
25
26
.
10. 1 Corinthians 9:9 / Deuteronomy 25:4
Locator: Page 349
27
.
Printed Text: ἐν γὰρ τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ γέγραπται· Οὐ ⸀κημώσεις βοῦν ἀλοῶντα. μὴ τῶν βοῶν μέλει τῷ θεῷ,
27
Apparatus Entry: 9 κημώσεις Treg NIV ] φιμώσεις WH RP
27
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Variant & Lexis: Significant lexical variation unit in the verb of prohibition: Holmes selects κημώσεις alongside Tregelles and NIV, rejecting φιμώσεις read by Westcott–Hort and the Byzantine textform (RP)
27
.
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Formal legal attribution ἐν γὰρ τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ γέγραπται· ending with a high point (·)
11
27
. Direct quotation opens with a capital letter (Οὐ)
12
27
.
Syntax: The prohibition clause Οὐ ⸀κημώσεις βοῦν ἀλοῶντα is closed with a full stop (.), separating the quotation from Paul's ensuing rhetorical question
27
.
11. 1 Corinthians 10:7 / Exodus 32:6
Locator: Page 350.
Printed Text: μηδὲ εἰδωλολάτραι γίνεσθε, καθώς τινες αὐτῶν· ὥσπερ γέγραπται· Ἐκάθισεν ὁ λαὸς φαγεῖν καὶ πεῖν, καὶ ἀνέστησαν παίζειν.
Apparatus Entry: NONE IN THIS SOURCE (no variation unit occurs at verse 7).
Discriminating Textual Features:
Citation Formula & Punctuation: Comparative introductory formula ὥσπερ γέγραπται· marked by a high point (·)
11
. Direct speech capitalized (Ἐκάθισεν)
12
.
Orthography: Prints the contracted aorist active infinitive form πεῖν (rather than πιεῖν), following Westcott and Hort's verb orthography
10
.
Syntax: Narrative quotation with a shift from a singular verb with collective noun (Ἐκάθισεν ὁ λαός) governing coordinate purpose/result infinitives (φαγεῖν καὶ πεῖν) to a plural verb (ἀνέστησαν) governing an infinitive (παίζειν).
12. Galatians 3:13 / Deuteronomy 21:23
Locator: Page 382
28
.
Printed Text: Χριστὸς ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου γενόμενος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα, ⸂ὅτι γέγραπται⸃· Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου,
28
Apparatus Entry: 13 ὅτι γέγραπται WH Treg NIV ] γέγραπται γάρ RP
29
.
Discriminating Textual Features:
Variant: Multiword variation unit ⸂ὅτι γέγραπται⸃ in the introductory formula: Holmes, WH, Tregelles, and NIV read the causal conjunction ὅτι γέγραπται, whereas Robinson–Pierpont (RP) reads γέγραπται γάρ
28
29
.
Punctuation: High point (·) placed after the formula
11
28
; direct quotation capitalized (Ἐπικατάρατος)
12
28
.
Syntax & Lexis: Verbatim quotation clause (Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου) is unanimous across all collated editions
28
29
; it features a nominal curse construction with πᾶς modifying ὁ κρεμάμενος, with no explicit agency phrase (such as ὑπὸ θεοῦ) in any witness
28
29
.
Would you like to examine how other Pauline Old Testament citations with recorded variants—such as Romans 3:10–18, Romans 9:33, or 1 Corinthians 15:54–55—are presented in the text and apparatus?
